findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify that the git-daemon fixture sets `uploadpack.allowFilter=true` at global (`--git-config uploadpack.allowFilter=true` on the daemon command line, or in a per-process `$HOME/.gitconfig`) rather than in the bare repo's local config, because repository-level `uploadpack.allowFilter` is silently ignored by git-daemon as a documented security measure.
evidence: Plan text: 'Integration tests start git daemon as a localhost subprocess with --export-all and --enable=upload-pack, serve a bare repo configured uploadpack.allowFilter=true'

Git source / Gitaly docs: 'this configuration variable is ignored if it is seen in the repository-level config (this is a safety measure against fetching from untrusted repositories)' — uploadpack.allowFilter must be set globally or passed to the daemon process, not in the bare repo's local config
Consequence: git-daemon silently ignores repository-level uploadpack.allowFilter, so the fixture may behave as if filtering is disabled, defeating the purpose of the contrast test
findings.finding: The plan specifies the git-daemon test fixture serves a 'bare repo configured uploadpack.allowFilter=true', but `uploadpack.allowFilter` set at the repository level is silently ignored by git-daemon as a security measure — it must be set at global config scope or injected into the daemon via `--git-config uploadpack.allowFilter=true`. If the integration test sets this config only in the repo's `.git/config`, the daemon will silently drop all filters without error (falling back to full fetches and warning 'filtering not recognized by server, ignoring'), causing the `blob:none` contrast test to produce false-positive results (both filtered and unfiltered paths fetch the same large packfile).
findings.location: Real-Git fixture and safety section: 'serve a bare repo configured uploadpack.allowFilter=true'
scenarios: Integration test sets uploadpack.allowFilter=true in the bare repo's local config; git-daemon serves the repo without filter support; both filtered and unfiltered fetches receive the full packfile; the size contrast assertion never fires correctly, producing a false-passing test
CI runner uses a Git version ≥2.18 where the behavior is confirmed; the silent ignore makes this a silent correctness failure with no obvious error message
findings.suggested_fix: In the fixture setup, pass the config to the daemon directly: `git daemon --git-config uploadpack.allowFilter=true --export-all ...` or write a temporary global gitconfig pointing `$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at it. Assert in the test that `git ls-remote --filter=blob:none git://localhost:PORT/repo` receives a capability advertisement containing 'filter' before running the size-contrast assertions.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the exact GIT_TRACE_PACKET line format for a client-sent filter packet (e.g., by running a minimal local test with `GIT_TRACE_PACKET=stderr git fetch --filter=blob:none ...` and inspecting actual output) and update the plan's assertion string from `fetch> filter blob:none` to the confirmed format before implementing the integration tests.
evidence: Plan text: 'Each trace must contain fetch> filter blob:none, and a known tickets blob must be absent before worktree materialization'
Git book (git-scm.com) GIT_TRACE_PACKET example: output lines use 'packet: git<' and 'packet: git>' prefixes, not 'fetch>' — the format is 'packet: <direction> <content>'

Git source fetch-pack.c: the filter line is written as packet_buf_write(req_buf, "filter %s", spec) — the actual packet content is 'filter blob:none', but GIT_TRACE_PACKET adds its own prefix that the plan's assertion string does not reflect
Git t5702.sh uses 'grep "fetch=.*filter" trace' and 'grep "version 2" trace' patterns — not the 'fetch> filter blob:none' literal
findings.finding: The plan mandates that integration tests assert `GIT_TRACE_PACKET` output contains the exact string `fetch> filter blob:none` to prove the filter was sent on the wire. However, the documented format for GIT_TRACE_PACKET output uses a `packet: git>` prefix (for client-sent lines) rather than `fetch>`, and protocol v2 fetch-pack writes the filter as a bare `filter <spec>` packet line. The exact string `fetch> filter blob:none` does not appear in any public Git documentation or test suite and is likely the wrong assertion pattern — tests checking for it may silently pass or fail depending on the Git version and protocol negotiated, and will be brittle across Git releases.
findings.location: Real-Git fixture and safety section: 'Each trace must contain fetch> filter blob:none'
scenarios: Test greps for 'fetch> filter blob:none' but GIT_TRACE_PACKET emits 'packet: git> filter blob:none'; grep never matches; test is either always-failing or the plan intends a different trace mechanism (GIT_TRACE2?) that was never specified
Git upgrades the protocol trace format slightly; the brittle string match breaks all three GIT_TRACE_PACKET-based ACs (named_origin_filter, direct_fetch_filter)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the git-daemon fixture to pass `--git-config=uploadpack.allowFilter=true` on the daemon command line (not set it in the bare repo's local config), so the daemon actually advertises the filter capability and the blob:none contrast test is meaningful.
evidence: Plan text: 'serve a bare repo configured uploadpack.allowFilter=true'

Git documentation: 'uploadpack.allowFilter — if this option is set, upload-pack will support partial clone and partial fetch object filtering. Ignored if git-daemon sees this in a repository-level config (security measure against untrusted repos)'

Existing tests/unit/test_snapshot_blobless_747f.py line 79 sets `uploadpack.allowFilter=true` in the local repo config of a non-daemon file:// fixture — the same pattern would fail if applied to a daemon-served repo
Evidence class: Verified — git-daemon's security restriction on per-repo uploadpack.allowFilter is documented behavior; the plan's fixture spec does not use --git-config on the daemon command line
Prior review cache .rebar/cache/plan-review/037b-879e-fe13-47d2/7438064f647f9885ca63.json corroborates this finding
findings.finding: The integration fixture specifies 'serve a bare repo configured uploadpack.allowFilter=true', but git-daemon silently ignores uploadpack.allowFilter when set in a repository's local .git/config as a security measure — the option must be supplied to the daemon process via '--git-config uploadpack.allowFilter=true' on the daemon command line (or in the global git config). If the fixture sets this only in the bare repo's local config, the daemon serves without filter capability, and both the filtered and unfiltered fetch paths receive the full packfile, making the size-contrast threshold assertions pass vacuously regardless of whether blob:none is honored.
findings.location: Real-Git fixture and safety section: 'Integration tests start git daemon as a localhost subprocess with --export-all and --enable=upload-pack, serve a bare repo configured uploadpack.allowFilter=true'
scenarios: Integration test inits bare repo, sets uploadpack.allowFilter=true in its .git/config, starts git daemon pointing at it; daemon ignores the setting; all fetches (with and without --filter=blob:none) receive the full packfile; the 131072 KiB threshold that should reject the unfiltered full-history fetch never fires; the test passes vacuously, giving false confidence that the CI guardrails work.
A developer running the integration suite locally against a system git that does not enforce the daemon security restriction may see green, while CI with a stricter git version fails differently.
findings.suggested_fix: In the fixture, start git daemon as: `git daemon --reuseaddr --base-path=<dir> --export-all --enable=upload-pack --git-config=uploadpack.allowFilter=true git://<path>` — this injects the setting into the daemon process scope rather than the per-repo config that daemon ignores.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether git fetch --filter=blob:none succeeds without extensions.partialClone on the ubuntu-latest git version (currently 2.43+), and if not, add 'git config extensions.partialClone origin' (or equivalent) before each direct-URL filtered fetch in gerrit-verify.yaml.
evidence: Plan text: 'Add --filter=blob:none explicitly to the depth-1 require-ticket fetch and to the full-history verify-identity fetch'
gerrit-verify.yaml lines 100-102: `timeout 60 git fetch --depth=1 'https://github.com/...' '+tickets:refs/remotes/gh-tickets'` — plan would add --filter=blob:none here
gerrit-verify.yaml lines 255-258: `git fetch 'https://github.com/...' '+tickets:refs/remotes/gh-tickets'` — plan would add --filter=blob:none here
Both Gerrit jobs use lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action@f87b90a3370e62dad310797fedc7fd3700c75832 (lines 70, 225), which does not set extensions.partialClone

git 2.42+ behavior: --filter on git fetch requires extensions.partialClone to be set in the client repo config; without it, git exits with 'fatal: --filter can only be used when extensions.partialClone is set'
ubuntu-latest currently ships git 2.43+, which is above the 2.42 threshold where this check was tightened

Evidence class: Partially-verified — the client-side extensions.partialClone guard is documented in git source and community reports, but its exact enforcement on ubuntu-latest runners is not confirmed by a live probe
findings.finding: The plan adds '--filter=blob:none' to direct-URL git fetch commands in the Gerrit verify-identity and require-ticket jobs, but those jobs use lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action (not actions/checkout with filter:), which does not initialize the repository with extensions.partialClone. On git >= 2.42 there is a documented client-side guard: 'fatal: --filter can only be used when extensions.partialClone is set', which fires when --filter is passed to git fetch in a workspace not initialized as a partial clone. The plan does not address whether GitHub.com's server-side filter capability advertisement alone bypasses this client-side check on the ubuntu-latest runner's git version, nor does it provide a mitigation (e.g., 'git config extensions.partialClone origin' before the filtered fetch, or 'git -c extensions.partialClone=origin fetch ...').
findings.location: Scope and mechanisms section (Gerrit paragraph): 'In .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml, named-remote inheritance does not apply because both tickets fetches use a direct URL. Add --filter=blob:none explicitly to the depth-1 require-ticket fetch and to the full-history verify-identity fetch'; gerrit-verify.yaml lines 100-113 (require-ticket step) and lines 255-267 (verify-identity step)
scenarios: ubuntu-latest runner ships git 2.43; Gerrit verify-identity job runs checkout-gerrit-change-action (no partial clone init); the subsequent 'git fetch --filter=blob:none https://github.com/...' fails with 'fatal: --filter can only be used when extensions.partialClone is set'; the job fails with a confusing error unrelated to authorship, not a size guard trip.
GitHub tightens runner git version and the previously passing Gerrit filter steps start failing, with no documented mitigation in the plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Before each filtered direct-URL fetch in the Gerrit jobs, add: `git config extensions.partialClone origin` (using a dummy remote name, since there is no named remote) or use `git -c extensions.partialClone=origin fetch --filter=blob:none <URL> ...` to satisfy the client-side guard without permanently altering the repo config.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the port-selection default in the fixture spec (e.g., 'bind to port 0 and read the OS-assigned port from the socket' or 'use a pytest-reserved ephemeral port') so parallel CI workers do not collide.
evidence: 'reserve a loopback port, and poll the socket with a bounded deadline before use' — no port-selection strategy stated

findings.finding: The integration fixture section says 'reserve a loopback port' for the git daemon subprocess but does not specify the reservation mechanism (OS-assigned port 0, a fixed port, a pytest-plugin allocation). A fixed port causes parallel CI worker collisions; the plan gives the executor no default to act on.
findings.location: Real-Git fixture and safety section — 'reserve a loopback port, and poll the socket with a bounded deadline before use'
scenarios: Two pytest-xdist workers both try to bind git daemon on the same hard-coded port; one fails with EADDRINUSE and the integration suite becomes flaky in parallel CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'reserve a loopback port' with 'bind git daemon to port 0, read the assigned port from the listening socket, and pass it to all client commands' — this is the idiomatic OS-assigned approach that avoids collisions without a plugin dependency.

findings.finding: The plan requires capturing GIT_TRACE_PACKET and asserting 'each trace must contain fetch> filter blob:none', but does not specify how GIT_TRACE_PACKET is set in the test subprocess (env-var to the git child process, GIT_TRACE_PACKET=/dev/stderr, a named temp file) or where the captured output is searched. findings.location: Real-Git fixture and safety section — 'Capture GIT_TRACE_PACKET for three fetch modes'
scenarios: Executor sets GIT_TRACE_PACKET=2 (stderr) and the test captures stdout only, never finding the packet string and producing a false-negative failure; alternatively, executor writes to a temp file but forgets to flush/close before asserting, causing intermittent misses.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'Set GIT_TRACE_PACKET=<tempfile.name> in the subprocess environment for each fetch invocation, then assert open(tempfile.name).read() contains "fetch> filter blob:none" before deleting the temp file.'

findings.suggested_fix: Extend `tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py` with a test keyed `-k size_pack` that: (1) spins up a local git daemon or subprocess git server with uploadpack.allowFilter=true, (2) clones with --filter=blob:none and fetch-depth=0 into a temp dir, (3) runs `git count-objects -v` and extracts `size-pack`, (4) asserts `size_pack_kib < 102400`. Update AC2's proving command to include `pytest tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py -k size_pack -v` alongside the existing unit test.

findings.finding: The size-pack guardrail failure path — the case where the filter is NOT applied and the pack exceeds the threshold, causing the job to fail — has no integration test. AC2's proving command (`-k size_pack`) is exclusively a unit test that parses the YAML for the presence of `git count-objects -v` and a failure threshold; it can only confirm the guardrail steps exist in the YAML, not that they fire correctly. No integration test constructs a repository whose unfiltered clone exceeds 102400 KiB or 131072 KiB and verifies the job actually fails, nor does any test confirm the guardrail passes on a genuine blobless fetch. This is a missing failure path for a new CI-user-facing behavior.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC2; Safety and observability §'Add measured guardrails'; proving command: pytest tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py -k size_pack -v
findings.suggested_fix: In tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py, add a parametrized test `test_size_pack_guardrail` that uses a local bare repo with a large blob (>102400 KiB when packed). Assert that a plain clone produces a size-pack above threshold, and that a blobless clone (`--filter=blob:none`) produces a size-pack below threshold. This gives the guardrail thresholds a live behavioral anchor without requiring GitHub Actions infrastructure.

findings.finding: The Gerrit direct-fetch path (`--filter=blob:none` added to two explicit `git fetch <url>` commands in gerrit-verify.yaml) has no protocol-level filter-application test equivalent to AC3's named-remote packet-trace assertion. AC3 proves `fetch> filter blob:none` appears in GIT_TRACE_PACKET for the named-remote inheritance path only; for the Gerrit direct-fetch path, live filter-application evidence is limited to AC4's reconverge success (which does not assert the filter was server-honored or that a known blob is absent before materialization). The direct-fetch path is the NEW DEFAULT for Gerrit CI and is the highest-risk cutover; its filter application is currently validated only by YAML structural inspection (AC1) and end-to-end reconverge success (AC4).
findings.location: Scope and mechanisms §'The Gerrit Verified workflow'; Acceptance Criteria AC1, AC3, AC4; gerrit-verify.yaml
